We need to generate a test class covering the given test cases. We have existing test class with two tests. Need to expand to cover all groups. Use parameterized tests where appropriate. Use JsonSchemaFactory to create schemas per test case group. Some cases involve expecting exceptions. Some involve different schemas (e.g., enum, pattern, number range, array constraints, nested object, $ref, multiple errors, null type, boolean, invalid $ref encoding, MissingNode, circular $ref, binary node). We'll need to create schemas accordingly in @BeforeEach or within each test method.

We should keep the existing @BeforeEach that builds a simple schema for name required. But many test cases need different schemas. We can create separate test methods that set up their own schema within the method.

We'll use JUnit5 @ParameterizedTest with @MethodSource providing arguments: rootNode JSON string, expected behavior (empty, non-empty, exception class). For groups with same schema, we can reuse.

We need to import necessary classes, including JsonSchemaFactory, VersionFlag, InputFormat maybe not needed.

We'll need to handle NullNode case: mapper.readTree("null") returns NullNode.

BinaryNode: use JsonNodeFactory.instance.binaryNode(new byte[]{1,2,3}).

MissingNode: JsonNodeFactory.instance.missingNode().

Invalid $ref encoding: need schema with $ref "#%ZZ". We'll create schema JSON string containing "$ref": "#%ZZ". Then schema.validate(rootNode) where rootNode maybe any, but we expect UnsupportedEncodingException. However validate(JsonNode) may wrap in RuntimeException; we can assertThrows(RuntimeException.class) and check cause.

Circular $ref: schema with "$ref": "#". This will cause recursion. Might cause StackOverflowError. We'll assertThrows(StackOverflowError.class) maybe.

Need to handle enum, pattern, number range, array constraints, nested object, $ref resolution, multiple errors, null type, boolean type.

We'll write helper method to parse JSON string to JsonNode.

We'll use static ObjectMapper.

We'll use @ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class) though not needed.

We'll keep existing tests.
